Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy destination calendars without credentialId, pre-refactor references) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback, so the event is never updated and the old time slot stays booked on the host's calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

Because this branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/""), the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` cannot match any real calendar externalId, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` instead of falling back to the event’s destination calendar externalId (previous behavior was effectively `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`). This makes updates for legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId` select no calendar (likely sending `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`), breaking reschedule/update behavior.
